question: A builder had 133 work items. He multiplied by 4 for crew members. He multiplied by 8 for hours per crew member. He divided by 2 for efficiency gains. He divided by 2 again for shared resources. He added 46 items from contingency (measured in total work items). His assistant added 9 items to the contingency list. What was the final contingency work item count?

On Monday morning a furniture factory ran 3 assembly lines, and each line produced 27 chairs for one batch. In the afternoon 67 chairs came back from a cancelled order and joined that same batch. Fitting each chair in the batch takes 7 screws. The contract covers 3 identical hotels, and every hotel receives a batch of exactly that size. That evening the storeman added 32 spare screws to the shipment. The factory van holds 40 boxes. How many screws are in the shipment?

A gardener had 110 seeds. They added 20 seeds. They divided into 5 rows equally. They removed 15 seeds that didn't sprout. They multiplied the remaining by 7 for planning. Morning planting, afternoon watering, evening checking. Someone had a dozen seeds (word count). How many seeds for growth?

Mia had 59 stickers, more than her classmate Jonah's 20. She earned 9 more for finishing her homework early. A teacher gave the whole class 18 more each, so she gained 18. A sticker-trading event multiplied her sheet fivefold. A mishap then cost her 404 stickers when a whole page fell into a puddle. She found 9 more in her backpack. Finally, a bonus round at recess multiplied her remaining stickers sixfold. How many stickers did Mia end up with?

Maria and James are comparing their project budgets. Maria starts with 130 dollars. She divides by 5 for her weekly allocation. She spends 6 dollars. She multiplies by 3 for monthly planning. She adds 68 dollars in additional funding. She multiplies by 6 for annual projections. She adds 10 dollars in interest. James has budgeted 200 dollars for his project. What is Maria's annual budget projection?

A tool library had 85 drills on its shelves, and a donation added 9 more. Members borrowed 55 drills, and 30 were sent away for servicing. A grant then paid for 7 drills for every drill still on the shelf. A hardware chain donated 20 further drills, and the library opens 4 days a week. How many drills are on the shelf now?

On Monday morning a warehouse held 210 sacks of rice, and a delivery added 10 more. At midday the stock was split evenly, and the manager kept half of the sacks at the main site while the rest went to a second store. During the afternoon 48 sacks were sold from the main site. Later that afternoon a returned order brought 63 sacks back to it. In the evening 68 sacks were driven from the main site to a food bank. How many sacks were left at the main site?

A charity tracked the total dollars raised in its online donation counter all week, starting at 83 dollars. A matching-donor program multiplied the counter by 4. A platform fee then took back a quarter of that, dividing the counter by 4 to reflect just the net amount kept — the treasurer noted this in her log as converting gross dollars to net dollars, a simple unit change. A refund request then removed 12 dollars from the net counter. A late donation added 15 more dollars. Finally, a corporate sponsor multiplied the net counter by 5. How many dollars did the net counter show by the end of the week?

In the morning, a warehouse had 218 boxes. By midday, half of the boxes were moved to another location. In the afternoon, 40 boxes were shipped out. By evening, 55 boxes arrived. That night, 4 more boxes were received. The next morning, 51 boxes were sent out. Converting to pallets (1 pallet = 2 boxes), how many boxes remain?

A honey farm had 101 jars of honey ready at the start of harvest. A bumper crop turned every jar into 9 jars. A second bumper crop turned each of those into 5 jars, a harvest that took '600 minutes, or ten hours' to bottle. A large wholesale order then took away 884 jars. A final matching order turned every remaining jar into 2 jars. How many jars of honey were left after the final matching order?

Early on Saturday morning Amira had 204 pots on her nursery bench, and she sold 85 of them straight away. Every pot still on the bench holds 5 seedlings. Her assistant Bruno, who had grown far fewer than Amira, added 26 loose seedlings from his own tray. During the afternoon a landscaper took 128 seedlings for a hedge planting. In the evening a school collected 157 more seedlings for its garden club. Amira has run this nursery for a dozen years. How many seedlings are left on the bench?

In the morning, a printing press had 182 orders queued, logged over 60 minutes, or 1 hour, of intake. By midday, six more matching intake batches made the queue seven times as large. In the afternoon, 282 orders were completed and removed from the queue. By evening, six more matching intake batches made the queue seven times as large again. Finally, 6,660 orders were completed overnight. How many orders were left in the queue?

A council depot had 178 bags of grit at the start of winter. A supplier delivered 17 bags, a neighbouring depot sent over 70, and a farmer returned 9 he had never used. The gritting lorries got through 234 bags during the long cold spell, and 13 bags split open in the rain and were wasted. The depot's records are kept in single bags rather than in tonnes. How many bags of grit are left?

A brewery has 237 barrels in the cellar and 57 more standing out in the yard. Every barrel is decanted into 4 kegs. A supplier then delivered 44 ready-filled kegs of the same size. Each keg fills 9 crates of bottles. The brewery's chimney is 22 metres tall. How many crates of bottles can the brewery fill?

A workshop started with 109 items. They tripled their stock. They spent 5 items for tools. They used 197 items in production. They used 86 more items. Their partner had 200 items. They multiplied by 8. How many items do they have?

In the morning, Tobias set out with 140 flyers for the town fair, more than the 120 flyers his friend Klara was carrying. By midday he had handed out 61 flyers. In the afternoon he handed out 65 more, and 6 blew away in the wind. The town has 30 streets. In the evening he returned the flyers he still had to the printer, who paid him 4 cents for every flyer returned. How many cents did the printer pay Tobias?

In the morning, a shop had 32 items. By midday, they added 42 items. By afternoon, they added 62 items. By evening, they tripled. They increased 8 times. They increased 4 times. Finally, they divided by half. Converting to dozens, how many items are there?

A gardener started with 82 flower pots. In the morning, 34 pots were removed for replanting. They multiplied the remaining by 6. Then added 71 pots of new plantings. Finally, they multiplied by 3 and then by 2 for seasonal expansion, converting to work hours. A botanical facility had 500 pots but separate garden. How many total pots after expansion?

A parcel depot took in 8 cages, each containing 105 parcels. The parcels were divided equally between 3 delivery rounds, and one driver loaded a single round's share into his van. The depot van park has 14 spaces. A late collection added 65 parcels to that driver's load. A load of that same size is now planned for each of the 8 drivers who work on Saturdays. How many parcels will the Saturday drivers carry in total?

Ida had 199 seed packets stored in her potting shed. Her neighbour Omar, whose shelf held far fewer than hers, gave her 33 packets he would never use, and the garden shop threw in 12 more with an order. Every packet held enough for 2 sowings, so Ida relabelled her stock as that many single sowings. She used 409 of the sowings across her beds in the spring, and 1 more was ruined when a mouse got into the shed. Late in the year she was given 22 further sowings by the allotment society. How many sowings did Ida have?

A farmer started with 152 apple trees. He added 23 new saplings to his orchard. He multiplied the rows by 7 for organization. He multiplied by 2 for split shifting work. He multiplied by 8 for seasonal expansion plans. He owned 5 other orchards across town. How many apple trees did the farmer manage in this location?

A warehouse had 146 boxes. They multiplied by 9. They multiplied by 8 again. They added 3 premium boxes. They removed 2083 items. They removed 1718 more. His coworker manages 50 boxes separately. How many boxes remain?

A construction site tracked the total feet of electrical wire on the main spool, starting with 225 feet. A first-floor wiring job used 189 feet. The remaining wire's tracked length was then tripled once a matching spool was added in. A second delivery added 38 more feet. A third delivery added 29 more feet. Converting the tracked length from feet to meters for the European supplier's invoice — a simple unit change — the crew subtracted 1 unit for a rounding correction. How many meters did the tracked total come to?

In the morning, a shop had 47 items. In the afternoon, they added 77 items. By evening, they added 41 items. They added 13 items. They removed 89 items. Finally, they added 34 items. How many items do they have?

A brickworks fired 72 racks in one week, with 4 trays on every rack and 3 bricks on every tray. A neighbour returned 25 bricks that had never been used on his extension. A garden wall job then took 529 bricks away from the yard. How many bricks are left at the works?
